FIX IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED AT THE CODE LEVEL. You took the corrected form, including the canonicalization I flagged late.

  .canonical_additive_weights(weights)
    -> as(weights, "CsparseMatrix") -> as(., "generalMatrix") -> Matrix::drop0()

  .canonical_additive_weight_identity(weights)
    -> canonicalize, coerce a base matrix to sparse if needed, then hash
       list(storage = "canonical_general_csparse", i, p, x, dim)

That is exactly the drop0 + pinned-representation form from my correction note, and tagging the storage kind in the hashed payload is a nice addition - it makes the signature self-describing rather than relying on an implicit convention.

All three sites are routed through the helper, and no as.matrix(frame$weights) remains anywhere in R/:
  measurement-decomposition.R:76, measurement.R:504, :507, :519, :558

SIGNATURE PROPERTIES VERIFIED on a small fixture:
  same frame built twice        -> identical signature   TRUE
  different searchlight radius  -> signatures differ     TRUE
  one weight perturbed by 1e-12 -> signatures differ     TRUE

So the canonicalization did not blunt sensitivity, and the signature is stable across independent construction of the same frame.

One incidental finding while testing: a frame whose stored weight is forced to zero is rejected earlier by .validate_frame_for_compile with "Locally normalized frame rows must sum to one", so a stored zero that changes the mathematics cannot reach the signature at all. The drop0 canonicalization is therefore belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing for locally normalized frames - still correct to have, and it matters for any future normalization mode that permits zero rows.

The p=50000 end-to-end reproduction is running now; the previous failure was at 55.9s inside plan_geometry and this run has passed that point without the allocation error. I will confirm the completed timing next pass.
